blocks.text: National Unit Pricing for Tenant Improvement Renovation Dust Cleanup

When a commercial tenant remodels an existing office—knocking down demising walls, upgrading conference room glass, sanding drywall patches, or replacing carpet tile with luxury vinyl plank—fine gypsum, wood, and silica particulates migrate far beyond the immediate work zone. Standard nightly janitorial pricing ($0.05 to $0.20 per square foot depending on building size bracket) is calibrated around light ambient soil and an ISSA production benchmark of 3,500 square feet per labor hour.

By contrast, tenant improvement (TI) renovation dust remediation demands top-to-bottom true-HEPA dry vacuuming of ceiling diffusers, light fixtures, vertical wall surfaces, window blinds, and furniture crevices, followed by two-bucket neutral-pH microfiber damp wiping to prevent white chalky streaks. Because technician production drops to 600–1,100 square feet per hour and requires commercial HEPA filter bags and specialty solvents, unit rates scale according to both total square footage and the depth of the renovation.

blocks.text: Per-Square-Foot vs. Hourly vs. Per-Fixture Pricing Models

Commercial cleaning contractors structure tenant improvement dust cleanup quotes using one of three pricing models depending on how clearly the general contractor or facility manager defines the architectural scope:

items: Fixed Per-Square-Foot Turnkey Bids ($0.14 to $0.55/sq ft): Preferred by corporate real estate teams and general contractors closing out a Tenant Improvement Allowance (TIA). The vendor inspects the floor plan and commits to a fixed lump sum covering all labor, HEPA consumables, and supervision required to pass the landlord's white-glove walk-through.

Time-and-Materials Hourly Billing ($55 to $95/hour per technician): Used when a renovation occurs in live, occupied offices over multiple weekend phases or when trades run behind schedule. Compare this specialty rate against standard commercial cleaning hourly rates of $35 to $65 per hour; the $20 to $30 hourly premium reflects certified HEPA equipment, personal protective equipment (PPE), and slower detail production.

Itemized Per-Fixture and Add-On Line Items: Frequently layered onto base square-foot bids when a remodel features dense architectural upgrades. Typical line-item add-ons include restroom deep descaling and fixture polishing ($35 to $75 per restroom fixture, compared to $15 to $30 per visit for routine restroom maintenance), interior glass partition razor-scraping and polishing ($25 to $55 per glass room, vs. $15 to $35 for routine glass wiping), and breakroom cabinetry interior vacuuming ($45 to $95 per breakroom, vs. $12 to $25 for standard breakroom sanitation).

blocks.title: Minimum Service & Dispatch Thresholds for Small TI Projects
blocks.text: While routine commercial office cleaning carries a standard minimum visit charge of $90 to $135, specialty renovation dust remediation carries a higher project minimum of $185 to $350 per mobilization. If you remodel a 900-square-foot executive conference room or wellness suite, expect a flat minimum mobilization fee rather than a straight $0.22-per-square-foot calculation, covering truck loading, HEPA machine transport, and two-person crew dispatch.

blocks.text: Equipment and Tool Standards That Prevent Post-Renovation Haze

A common failure during tenant improvement cleanups occurs when an under-equipped crew uses standard janitorial string mops and non-sealed vacuums on drywall dust. Standard paper vacuum bags allow sub-micron gypsum particles to blow straight through the motor exhaust back into the breathing zone, while a dirty mop bucket spreads a thin white film across dark LVT or ceramic tile that reappears as soon as the floor dries.

Professional remediation crews deploy stage-specific commercial tools from initial debris pickup through final executive touch-ups. During the rough perimeter and entry sweep, technicians use the Unger Nifty Nabber 36-Inch Commercial Trash Picker Grabber (with its 36-in Reach, rubber-coated Steel Claws, Ergonomic trigger handle, and 10 lb Lift rating) to clear drywall shims, wire clippings, and packaging scraps from radiator troughs and planter boxes without hand injuries. For continuous dry debris containment in active corridors without raising airborne dust clouds, day porters rely on the Rubbermaid Commercial Lobby Pro Upright Dust Pan & Broom (featuring a Long Handle, self-opening Auto Lid that conceals construction grit, Quiet Wheels, and a durable Day Porter duty profile). Finally, during the white-glove walk-through and executive-suite punch list, supervisors deploy the Dyson V15 Detect Pro / Commercial Spot Cordless Stick (engineered with a full-machine HEPA Seal, green Laser Detect optic head that reveals microscopic drywall film on hard floors, 60 min Run time, and lightweight 6.8 lb frame) to capture lingering sill, drawer-track, and baseboard dust instantaneously.
Step-by-Step Budgeting Workflow for Facility & Project Managers

To keep your tenant improvement cleaning invoice within budget and avoid change-order disputes between the general contractor and your building's base janitorial provider, follow this four-step procurement sequence:

items.name: Define the Demarcation Line Between GC Rough Sweep and Specialty Dust Remediation
items.text: Verify in your construction contract whether the general contractor's 'broom-clean' turnover clause includes true-HEPA high dusting and interior millwork wiping. If it only covers bulk trash removal, allocate $0.22 to $0.35 per square foot in your TI budget for an independent janitorial detail clean.

items.name: Measure Adjacent Drift Zones Beyond the Construction Barrier
items.text: Even with zippered plastic dust walls, fine dust migrates 25 to 50 feet down shared corridors, elevator lobbies, and return-air plenums. Add 15% to 25% of your remodeled square footage as an adjacent light-remediation zone ($0.10 to $0.18 per square foot).

items.name: Require Two-Pass Wet Microfiber Rinse Verification on Hard Floors
items.text: Specify in the work order that all VCT, LVT, and tile floors must receive a clean-water microfiber flat-mop rinse pass after initial scrubbing, inspected under full overhead LED lighting once completely dry to guarantee zero chalky gypsum haze.

items.name: Hold Back 20% of the Budget for a 72-Hour Post-HVAC Settling Pass
items.text: Once the building's HVAC system runs at normal occupancy airflow for three days, residual dust trapped in supply ducts will settle onto desk surfaces. Schedule a fast follow-up 'puff clean' ($0.06 to $0.12 per square foot) before employees unpack personal items.

blocks.title: OSHA Silica & Indoor Air Quality Compliance During Occupied Remodels
blocks.text: When tenant improvements involve cutting concrete slabs, drilling masonry, or sanding joint compound adjacent to occupied office wings, OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1153 strictly prohibits dry sweeping or compressed-air blowing of dust. Ensure your cleaning contractor utilizes sealed HEPA-filtration vacuums (99.97% efficiency at 0.3 microns) and maintains SDS documentation on site for any citrus adhesive removers or neutral-pH detergents.

faqs.q: Who pays for tenant improvement renovation dust cleanup: the landlord, the general contractor, or the tenant?
faqs.a: If the build-out is managed by the landlord's construction team under a turnkey work letter, basic rough and final cleaning is usually funded out of the Tenant Improvement Allowance (TIA). However, general contractor 'final cleans' often leave behind fine gypsum haze inside cabinets, on glass partitions, and in adjacent occupied suites. Tenants frequently contract their own commercial janitorial vendor directly for a $0.14 to $0.25 per square foot white-glove detail pass before moving computers and staff in.

faqs.q: Why does renovation dust reappear on desks two days after a professional cleanup?
faqs.a: Fine drywall and plaster dust particles measuring under 5 microns remain suspended in still room air for up to 48 hours and also accumulate inside overhead return-air plenums and HVAC supply diffusers. When the HVAC system cycles on, those particles settle onto freshly wiped horizontal surfaces. Replacing return-air filters immediately after the final clean and scheduling a lightweight follow-up microfiber dust pass 48 to 72 hours later eliminates the recurring haze.

faqs.q: Can we just pay our regular nightly cleaning crew a few extra hours to handle renovation dust?
faqs.a: Usually yes for light cosmetic work, provided your vendor dispatches a dedicated project crew equipped with commercial HEPA vacuums and high-reach tools billed at specialty hourly rates ($55 to $95/hr). Relying on the standard nightly maintenance worker during their regular shift fails because their routine time allocation is based on 3,500 square feet per hour and standard vacuum filters will quickly clog or blow fine gypsum dust back into the suite.

faqs.q: How do we transition a newly renovated floor plate into our recurring monthly janitorial billing?
faqs.a: Once the one-time TI dust remediation invoice is closed out, the renovated square footage is folded into your ongoing service agreement using standard commercial size brackets (for example, $0.09 to $0.15 per square foot for 2,500–9,999 sq ft, or $0.07 to $0.12 per square foot for 10,000–24,999 sq ft) multiplied by your visit frequency across 4.33 weeks per month.
